items.text: Geometric notions over a field $k$
Geometrically reduced = separable; geometrically integral = geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible; geometrically connected.

$X$ geometrically connected over $k$ iff $X\times Y$ connected for every connected $Y$, iff $X_{k'}$ connected for every extension $k'$, iff $X_{\bar k}$ connected. Gap: show that "$X_{k'}$ connected for every finite separable $k'/k$" implies this ($k_1=\varinjlim k_i$).

Case $X$ locally of finite type over $k$ (locally noetherian): $U_1\subset X_{k_1}$ open and closed; its image $U_i\subset X_{k_i}$ is closed ($k_1/k_i$ integral, so closed after base change) and stable under generalisation (flat); with finitely many components locally, $U_i$ is open and closed, so empty or all of $X_{k_i}$; hence $U_1=\varnothing$ or $X_{k_1}$.
General case: use that $X_{k_1}\to X_{k_i}$ is open.
A morphism to the spectrum of a field is universally open.
$f\colon X\to S$ locally of finite presentation and flat $\Rightarrow$ $f$ open (to be proved later).
Reduce to $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$: $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ open; write $A=\varinjlim A_i$ (finite presentation), $X'=\varprojlim X'_i$.
Lemma. $X'=\varprojlim X'_i$ over $S'$; if each $X'_i\to S'$ is open and the transition maps $X'_j\to X'_i$ are fibrewise dominant, then $X'\to S'$ is open.
U=p_i^{-1}(U_i),\qquad f_i(U_i)=f(U)\ \Longrightarrow\ f(U)\ \text{open}
Geometric connectedness from one point

Statement. $f\colon Z\to X$ with $X$ connected, $Z$ geometrically connected and non-empty. Then $X$ is geometrically connected. (The analogue for irreducible needs a further hypothesis: see the correction of 2 July.)
In particular if $X$ has a rational point (take $Z=\operatorname{Spec}k$).

Proof: enough for $k'/k$ finite Galois, group $\Pi$ acting on $X_{k'}$. $U\subset X_{k'}$ open and closed, non-empty; $Z_{k'}$ connected, so (up to complement) $U\supset\operatorname{Im}Z_{k'}$; $Z_{k'}$ is $\Pi$-stable, so

V=\bigcap_{g\in\Pi}gU\ \text{open and closed, }\Pi\text{-stable, containing }\operatorname{Im}Z_{k'};\qquad X=X_{k'}/\Pi\Rightarrow V=\text{preimage of an open-closed subset of }X,\ \text{non-empty, so}\ V=X_{k'}
The neutral component

$G$ a group over $k$: the unit $\operatorname{Spec}k\to G$ is a rational point, so $G$ connected $\Rightarrow$ geometrically connected. $G^0$ = connected component of the unit (with the reduced structure) is geometrically connected.
(i) $G^0$ open (e.g. $G$ locally of finite type, so locally noetherian): with the induced open structure, $G^0$ is an open subgroup of $G$.
Proof: $G^0\times G^0$ is connected (geometrically connected), contains $(e,e)$, so its image under the law lies in $G^0$; same for $g\mapsto g^{-1}$.
(ii) $k$ perfect: $G^0_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $G$.
Proof: $G'\times G'$ is reduced ($k$ perfect), and a morphism from a reduced scheme into $Y$ factors through a closed subscheme $Y'$ as soon as it does so set-theoretically.
Likewise $G_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a subgroup of $G$ ($k$ perfect).
